🌊 As we mark #WorldOceansDay and the launch of the 2025 UN Ocean Conference in Nice, we have a pivotal opportunity: to align ocean health with the global energy transition.

The ocean is a foundation of life on Earth. It covers 75% of the planet; generates 50% of our oxygen; absorbs 30% of CO2 emissions; and supports +150 million jobs worldwide. It provides food, energy and critical resources to billions - yet remains under threat from rising temperatures, acidification, pollution, overexploitation and biodiversity loss.

If the ocean economy were a country, it would be the fifth largest economy in the world. That level of economic and environmental significance calls for bold, integrated responses. Here’s where development action can accelerate meaningful impact:

1️⃣ Decarbonize Maritime Transport as a Catalyst for Clean Energy Systems:
Maritime transport emits over 1GtCO2 annually (around 2.9% of global emissions) and is one of the hardest sectors to decarbonize due to fossil fuel reliance and long asset lifecycles. To align with the Paris Agreement, zero-emission fuels need to make up 5% of international and 15% of domestic shipping by 2030. Transitioning to clean fuels can transform shipping from a major emitter into a catalyst for clean energy investment, innovation, and industrial demand, contributing directly to system-wide decarbonization and reducing global GHG emissions by 3-5% by 2030. 

2️⃣ Transform Ports into Clean Energy Hubs for a Just Transition:
Strategic clean fuel corridors can anchor renewable deployment, storage and grid upgrades at ports - especially in Small Island Developing States, where ocean-based exports account for 16% of GDP. Port electrification enhances climate resilience, connects maritime and energy planning, and ensures vulnerable economies benefit from the energy transition.

3️⃣ Integrate Maritime Decarbonization into Global Energy Finance:
Despite their potential, maritime and ocean-based clean energy solutions remain underfunded. In 2022, global clean energy investments reached  $2.1 trillion; yet < 1% was directed towards maritime energy developments. Offshore wind alone could grow from $39.6B in 2024 to $146B by 2031, powering up to 1.5B homes annually by 2050 and driving inclusive growth across coastal regions - especially in the Global South. Targeted funding through green bonds, blended finance, and multilateral support can unlock scalable pathways for maritime decarbonization and clean energy innovation at sea.

Decarbonization is critical, not only for SDG 13  and SDG 14, but for resilient, inclusive development. 

As we look toward this 2025 UN Ocean Conference, we must raise ambition; align public and private finance; and unlock innovation across the blue economy. A healthy ocean is not only vital for biodiversity. It is fundamental to a just energy transition

The ocean cannot wait - and neither can we.
